prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1334; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by the third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness, with onset within the first hour after the collision. No attorney representation noted at intake.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes whiplash-type symptoms, including limited neck rotation and headache. Claimant has not yet seen a physician and was advised to get evaluated and keep all treatment records. Claimant indicated they are handling the claim directly and do not have legal counsel.

Entry 3: Photos of both vehicles received from claimant. Rear bumper damage visible on the claimant's vehicle, consistent with the reported impact. Repair estimate requested from preferred shop. Liability appears clear based on the statement from the other driver and the police report narrative.

Entry 4: Claimant submitted initial medical visit summary. Diagnosis listed as cervical strain consistent with whiplash. Prescribed physical therapy and over-the-counter pain relief. Requested authorization for therapy sessions, which was reviewed under the medical payments coverage and approved on a per-visit basis.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant. Reports neck pain is improving but still present with prolonged sitting. Attending physical therapy as scheduled. Explained the claims process, the steps for submitting bills and mileage for reimbursement, and the timeline for a settlement review once treatment concludes. Claimant has no questions at this time. File remains open pending final medical records.
